findings.reason: §3 exists so §4 starts from a checkpoint that covers the cohort work; as wired, the one ordering that makes the checkpoint useful is the one the plan does not require, and a restore after §4 would silently lose §2's produced sources.
findings.text: plan-section-depends-on gives s3 only sn-integrity-backlog#s52 and not s2, so §3's checkpoint can legally be taken before §2 writes the graph; §3's done-when requires only that the checkpoint postdate "the last graph write of every §52 run", so a checkpoint taken between §2's dispatch and its run would satisfy §3 and still predate every name §2 produced

findings.reason: at the measured yield the run could spend its whole limit, exhaust all 828 sources, land near +180 and have no stated outcome, leaving the node blocked with unspent budget and the coordinator to rediscover the sizing the plan should have stated.
findings.text: the required accepted count of 5,503 is +300 over the 5,203 baseline, drawn from at most 828 sources (the 920 unaccepted less the 92 excluded vocabulary-gap class), a required yield of 36.2%; the census's own cost basis records the full run creating 284 accepted names over 1,308 eligible sources, a yield of 21.7%, and the 828 are that run's leftovers rather than a fresh population; §4 states an escalation only for a run that "would need more" (spend), not for exhausting the advanceable classes short of the floor

findings.reason: the diagnosis can be delivered while the restoration is unfunded ("§5 is expected to need the lead's spend ruling"), and vice versa, so one node cannot close on one verdict and its gate proves neither half; splitting the diagnosis as its own sized node would let it land without the spend ruling.
findings.text: §5's done-when binds two independent deliverables into one verdict: restoring accepted documentation to at least 2,368 among accepted names, and naming "the mechanism that lowered accepted documentation during the 2026-11-11 drain ... with evidence", which the section's own text says §52 is separately investigating and which §5 may have to derive itself

response_events.note: §3 now waits on §2 as well as on the §52 writers, so the checkpoint covers the cohort's produced sources.

§4's done-when now accepts, in place of the +300 floor, that every source in the advanceable classes was run with its outcome recorded and the shortfall against 5,503 reported with the measured yield, so a run that exhausts its classes first has a stated endpoint.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — sn-integrity-backlog §51/§52, sn-catalog-consistency §2, and the cited sib-docs-drain-after-admission.html all resolve; the plan carries no hrefs needing the .html convention.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — all four buildable sections declare a negative control that can fail (§2 planted unproduced source, §3 truncated archive, §4 planted out-of-class source, §5 planted pending-documentation name plus a before/after demotion read), and each measure is a count or a receipt identity.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — every section records under docs/evidence/fragments/sn-full-dd-continuation/, the repository's existing fragment convention, and no gate writes to a scratchpad or node-local path.
rubric_items.naming: pass — the plan names no new symbol, file or function, and carries no plan labels, ticket numbers or changelog prose into code.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §4's accepted-count floor requires a per-source yield 1.7x the rate the same census measured on a fresh population, and the plan names no outcome for exhausting the advanceable sources short of it.
rubric_items.single_goal: a finding — §5's done-when carries both a documentation-restoration threshold and a separate causal diagnosis of the drain.
rubric_items.wiring: a finding — the section-dependency map gives §3 no dependency on §2, so the checkpoint can be taken before §2's graph writes.
